title: Dependent Type Copy-Paste (Loss of Proof Constraint)
damaged_code:
```coq
(* Coq *)
match n with
| O => fun => Reduce (P1 dec "" && P2 dec s)
| S n' => fun => (P1 dec (substring 0 (S n') s) && P2 dec (substring (S n') (length s - S n') s)) || F n'
end
```
pattern: Duplicating complex type structures (e.g., repeating `S n'` instead of using a unified binder variable `n`) inside branches because the type-checker fails to carry over structural constraints.
why_bad: It degrades code maintainability. Copy-pasting long structural branches increases code volume and prevents centralized optimization.
detection: Duplicate pattern definitions inside nested branches of dependent match statements.
fix:
Bind the branch variable or use helper definitions to hide duplicate structural terms.
```coq
match n with
| O => fun => Reduce (P1 dec "" && P2 dec s)
| S n' => fun => let n := S n' in (P1 dec (substring 0 n s) && P2 dec (substring n (length s - n) s)) || F n'
end
```
